posts.cooked:
Making bread again. Here’s what I’ve been using. Basically it’s the recipe Mirasol posted a while back, but with variations because I’m adding whole wheat flour.

To make enough for a bread and a small pizza crust:
450 g all purpose flour
250 g whole wheat flour
2 T wheat gluten
2 t instant yeast
2 t kosher salt
18-22 oz warm water (maybe more?)

Mix all the dry ingredients, then mix in the water. Cover and let it sit 15 minutes - whole wheat flour takes a bit to fully hydrate. After the 15 minutes, mix it up a bit more. If you used more water, you can probably kind of shove it around with a spoon. If you used less, do a few stretch and folds (which is kind of a very basic knead you can do in the bowl). Then leave it to rise for two hours - from here it’s basically the same as the no-knead recipe Mirasol posted, which I will try to find the link for.

After the rise, I pull off about a pound (450 g) of the dough and put it in an oiled container and refrigerate until time to make pizza. (You can refrigerate before making the bread, too.) I’m not really satisfied with my pizza results yet. It’s hard to make this dough lie flat with hand shaping, so I’m basically winding up with a thin-ish loaf of bread made into pizza - it tastes good, but isn’t how I want my pizza. In any case, take it out of the fridge 30 minutes before baking, and unless you get it really thin, bake it most of the way without toppings, then let it cool a bit, before adding toppings and baking again. Otherwise the thick crust will still be raw inside when the cheese starts burning.

I think I need to either knead it, or use a rolling pin to flatten it out properly, or possibly both, to use this recipe for pizza. Today’s batch is wetter than my last, which may also help. I think last time I used around 19 oz of water, and this time it was closer to 22. I’m not sure exactly - I have a 2 cup measuring cup, and that (16 oz, a little under 1/2 liter) is definitely not enough, so I add more a couple of ounces at a time. No-knead bread has to be wetter (“high hydration” is apparently what bakers call it) than a dough you plan to knead.

You can use formulas and all, but I’m learning by trying. It’s an adventure!

Edit: I think this is the one Mirasol posted:
https://www.recipetineats.com/easy-yeast-bread-recipe-no-knead/
And if you like the scientific approach, there’s this one from Kenji López-Alt, which is pretty similar:
https://www.seriouseats.com/better-no-knead-bread-recipe

You don’t need to remove it from the original phone AFAIK. I have the Battle.net app on two different devices and used the restore code from the original device to sync the authenticator to the new device which is now a backup of the original. As long as you have the serial number and restore code you should be able to have the authenticator on any number of devices. It’s the SMS portion of the security measures that is tied to a single number.

If your new device is an Android phone or tablet, you may run into the dreaded infinite login loop though. The fix for that seems to be setting the default browser to Chrome temporarily (if you use say, Firefox), logging in, and then you can change the browser back to whatever you like, only needing to do the switchover when you have to re-enter your login credentials, which shouldn’t be too often as the Battle.net app for all its faults (and it has many), tends to stay logged in for a very long time.

I’m not sure what to do.

Right now? Get something to eat and some water. Breathe. Focus on what you see, hear, and can touch right in front of you. This second. Keep breathing. Eat some more.

Once the panic stops a bit realize that what your brain is doing is called catastrophizing. Making the WORST situation possible from a few tiny unrelated threads. It is not real. It won’t happen. It is a function of the jerk part of your brain and is scary and overwhelming. It is intrusive and unwanted. Completely not rational.

Are you even supposed to be at the IT conference? If so, text someone who you know and ask for info about it. If you were not tasked to go, then head back to the office, complete the tickets you can, and leave good notes for those with the power to handle the escalated ones.

Then - when work is done go home and focus on your garden. Do ONE thing - draw out where you want to put things, or mark out a garden edge, make up a list of supplies, etc. Just one thing you can say “I did this thing today and that is progress”.

Continue breathing and don’t listen to the jerk part of your brain. I am autistic too. Not fitting is ok. You are very good at different things and you fit just fine here

posts.name: pharazon
posts.cooked:
Guuah:

I recognize it’s my brain partually churning out these thoughts. I recognize it and yet I’m still freaking out. I don’t know what to do.

I don’t have any additional advice for grounding beyond what Mirasol has said. Racing anxiety, anxiety loops, catastrophizing are par for the course for me with occasional full panic, but even with various learned grounding techniques and medication, I’m not good at managing even if I good at recognizing it happening.

Hopefully, others’ advice here has been helpful, but one thing else is to not beat yourself up over the anxiety either. I know it’s easy to put ourselves down for what we ourselves may see as a failure to deal with anxiety and panic, even if it’s a time when the fear is irrational. Just remember that it’s okay to not be perfect at managing anxiety at any given time; none of us are: there’s no magic wand to wave and dissipate it every time.

You are awesome, and I enjoy reading your post. And, it’s okay not to fit into the mold of “normal” person, which I’m not sure what normal is to be honest because I certainly don’t fit that either.

Guuah:

I need to get into the habit of making my own breakfast

Just remember, anything can be your breakfast - most “breakfast” stuff isn’t all that healthy. But oatmeal is pretty quick and easy. And you can make it ahead. I’ve been known to make a batch of steel cut oats (my preferred choice), put them into a muffin tin, freeze, then move into Ziplocs. Throw one or two in a bowl, microwave, add fresh/dried fruit, nuts, brown sugar, and you’ve got a decent breakfast.

And make sure you have time to relax for a bit with breakfast. I try to set aside an hour to get ready for work and have breakfast sitting down at the table before I have to start (or leave for) work. It helps me feel less rushed. And getting to the office early helps with that, too. Plus it always gave me a chance to say good morning to my co-workers and get set up before clocking in.

I got to put my laundry out on the line today. Which means, with the sun and breeze, it was dry within about an hour and a half, instead of the hours it would take putting everything on the drying rack in the house.

That exercise can be really helpful and it is what I was referring Guuah to without going into it. I am really glad you posted the whole thing!

In addition to the 5 senses thing, they usually recommend literally placing your feet flat on the ground, hands flat on your legs or chair. Grounding your body in addition to your mind.

Remembering all that when you are panicking is not so easy though!

Guuah:

Head kinda hurts and feel a bit dizzy but think that’s normal?

Not really. It is not unusual though if your blood sugar is low or you are dehydrated. Those are the most common causes of being a bit lightheaded. The other is blood pressure dropping for some other reason besides dehydration.

Have some water!

Breakfast does not have to be breakfast food. You can:

  • Make a sandwich the night before, grab some fruit, take some granola bars with you. Eat that for breakfast and/or a snack.
  • You can even pre-make breakfast sandwiches (not exactly super healthy) and freeze or refrigerate them. Quick microwave zap and it is warm. English muffins or even just toast with cheese, egg, and meat (ham is easier and does not need cooking). Then all you need to do is make eggs and prep several for a few days.
  • Oatmeal with dried fruit and nuts is actually healthy as long as you don’t overdo the sugar.
  • Heck, you can even have dinner leftovers for breakfast.
  • Whole wheat bagel with cream cheese, fruit, and yogurt is healthy.
